channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: How the OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs Could Lift the Veil on AI Economics
item.description: VistaShares portfolio manager and DVX Ventures principal David Fetherstonhaugh says investors are increasingly looking for proof that massive AI spending is generating returns. He discusses why private companies like OpenAI and Anthropic leave a key part of the AI economy opaque and how their eventual IPOs could bring greater transparency to the ecosystem. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cisco, Nvidia Tackle AI’s Growing Data Center Bottleneck
item.description: Cisco is partnering with Nvidia on a new generation of optical networking technology designed to handle the exploding amount of data moving through AI data centers. Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel explains why increasingly powerful AI agents could consume far more network bandwidth than humans performing the same tasks, and how faster, more power-efficient connections could help hundreds of thousands of GPUs operate together while lowering the cost of AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fidelity: Tech Stocks Can Keep ‘Climbing the Wall of Worry’
item.description: Fidelity’s Denise Chisholm says technology stocks have undergone an unusually large valuation reset even as earnings expectations continue to rise, potentially leaving the sector positioned for further gains. She discusses why tech’s roughly 30% multiple contraction may already reflect concerns about slowing AI and technology spending, and why historical data suggests a slowdown in tech capex doesn’t necessarily mean a contraction. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft, Musk Race to Reinvent the AI Chip
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Microsoft's latest homegrown Maia chips, its latest effort to rely less on outside semiconductors to power its AI ambitions. Plus, Elon Musk wants to put chip development on fast-forward, testing as many as ten new designs a year; and Apple is finally ready to unveil its new smart home strategy, seeking to plug a major hole in its ecosystem. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Ramps Up Homegrown AI Chip Push
item.description: Microsoft is installing the latest version of its Maia chips in data centers to power its AI software using mostly homegrown hardware. The company expects to stock multiple gigawatts of its Maia chips, with the Maia 300 starting to roll out next year. Bloomberg's Matt Day joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Big Tech Is Borrowing Billions to Fund AI Spending
item.description: For the past few years, the largest US technology companies have been in a costly race to develop advanced artificial intelligence systems while at the same time providing computing power to a burgeoning field of startups. To chase these goals, they have radically changed how they finance their growth. Long reliant on rich revenues and share price increases, Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Meta Platforms Inc. and other tech giants now are borrowing heavily to build the technology that makes chatbots run
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo and Davide Barbuscia

item.title: Meta Says New Muse Model Reaches AI Frontier After Aggressive Push
item.description: The Muse Wonder model will be a key test for Meta’s expensive and rebuilt superintelligence team.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: OpenAI Adds New Irish Roles in Boost to Firm’s EU Headquarters
item.description: OpenAI announced it would add new jobs in Dublin, a further sign of rapid growth at the ChatGPT-maker’s European headquarters.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Fletcher

item.title: Ray-Ban Heir Details Drug Abuse, Escalates EssilorLuxottica Spat
item.description: EssilorLuxottica SA heir Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio publicly disclosed his challenges with drug addiction and renewed his criticism of the eyewear company’s leadership after stepping down from his executive roles in August.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Albanese

item.title: Why Gold Is Stuck Right Now
item.description: Gold’s rally is stalling as the Fed stays hawkish and real yields climb, squeezing one of the market’s favorite safe havens. Bloomberg’s Frank Monkam breaks down why volatility in gold has collapsed, what the tight gold–silver spread is really signaling and how copper has quietly become a high‑beta proxy on the AI trade and equity markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic AI Model Goes Rogue, Gives Cops a Fake Tip
item.description: Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model went rogue and carried out unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations. In one example, the AI model gave police in Philadelphia a fake tip on a homicide case. The police took no action. Other unintended behaviors were also noted. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Banks Poised to Surprise Wall Street: Analyst
item.description: Baird Senior Research Analyst David George joins Bloomberg Open Interest to lay out why he’s bullish on upcoming bank earnings despite a risk‑off market. He explains how AI-driven capital markets may cool, why regional banks could outperform the Wall Street giants, and how post‑election consolidation and higher rates set up JPMorgan and others for upside this quarter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: IonQ's Biggest Move Yet: A $1.3B Security Acquisition
item.description: IonQ, a major quantum leader, is making a blockbuster security acquisition. The company is buying cybersecurity company Elisity in a deal worth up to $1.3 billion. IonQ Chairman & CEO Niccolo de Masi joined Bloomberg Open Interest to talk about why the deal is key to defending the West from “Q-Day,” when quantum computers can crack today’s encryption. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman, Morgan Stanley Traders Are Split Over Virgin Media Debt
item.description: Traders at Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are split over the value of Virgin Media O2’s battered bonds, which plunged deep into distressed territory this month.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Morpurgo and Edward Clark

item.title: AI Markups Distorting 'True Earnings Power of S&P,' Says Larry McDonald
item.description: Stocks fluctuated near their all-time highs as traders looked ahead to the start of the earnings season and inflation data that will be key in shaping the Federal Reserve outlook. Larry McDonald, founder at The Bear Traps Report, discusses bond market stress, equity moves, and how AI related mark-ups are distorting S&P 500 earnings potential. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: T-Mobile Rises on Upgrade; IonQ to Buy Elisity | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Amazon (AMZN) shares are moving on news it's in negotiations to acquire Decart AI, an artificial intelligence startup, in a deal that could be valued at around $7 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported. The purchase could be wrapped up soon if the negotiations don’t collapse, the Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter. - IonQ (IONQ) shares are moving after it agreed to buy Elisity for as much as $1.3 billion in an all-stock transaction to expand its cybersecurity platform. IonQ Chief Executive Officer Niccolo de Masi said the company will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era. - T-Mobile (TMUS) shares are rising after Raymond James upgraded the stock to outperform from market perform, noting that the recent pullback in shares has created a buying opportunity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: How OpenAI’s Rogue Model Hacked Hugging Face
item.description: On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, Nate Soares, president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, joins Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway to talk about how a rogue OpenAI model hacked Hugging Face and why he thinks humanity's demise in the hands of superintelligent AI is inevitable. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dangote Refinery Extends IPO by Two Weeks on Strong Demand
item.description: Aliko Dangote plans to extend the deadline for applications for the initial public offering in his Nigerian refinery by two weeks as Africa’s richest man seeks to provide investors in more countries access to the continent’s biggest listing to date.
item.dc:creator: Loni Prinsloo and Emele Onu

item.title: Apollo's Slok on Housing, US Economic Growth, Fed Policy
item.description: Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok talks about the impact of higher interest rates on the US housing supply. He also discusses the prospects of an AI-induced bank run and which parts of the economy are the most sensitive to Federal Reserve interest rate moves. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hackers Hit French Supermarkets in Attack Disabling Fridges
item.description: Hundreds of supermarkets in France were hit by cyberattacks on Sunday night that disabled refrigeration systems and forced stores to throw out damaged food, following warnings that hackers are seeking to cause physical damage.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Che and Ryan Gallagher
